title: Fitting a 140 GB AI on a laptop
hook: Fit a 140 GB AI on a laptop

beats.say: A seventy billion parameter AI model needs about a hundred and forty gigabytes of memory.
Because every parameter is a number, stored with sixteen bits of precision.
Quantization rounds those numbers off. Fewer bits per number, way less memory.
At four bits, the same model shrinks to about thirty five gigabytes.
You lose a little accuracy, but it runs on a well-equipped laptop. Offline. Private.
That's how people run open models at home. Round the numbers, shrink the AI.

caption: Model memory ≈ parameters × bytes per parameter. A 70B model at 16-bit (2 bytes) needs ~140 GB. Quantization stores each weight with fewer bits: ~70 GB at 8-bit, ~35 GB at 4-bit, with a small accuracy cost. That's how open models run locally on laptops with tools like Ollama and llama.cpp.
sources: Arithmetic: 70e9 params × 2 bytes = 140 GB; × 0.5 byte = 35 GB (weights only, excludes runtime overhead)
